subject: Acme Security: SIG data-handling follow-up and evidence
messages:
From: security@acme.com
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG — few clarifying Qs on data retention and training

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for sending the completed SIG spreadsheet yesterday — we skimmed it and have a couple quick clarifications on the 'Data Handling' section before we move to procurement:

1) Prompt logs: can you confirm how long prompt and response logs are retained for hosted customers versus dedicated/private deployments?
2) Model training: the SIG matrix indicates "no customer data used for model training" — please confirm whether any pseudonymized or aggregated customer outputs could be used for research or model improvement.
3) Evidence: your SOC2 doc is helpful. Any light-weight artifacts we can share with our InfoSec team (one-pagers, retention policy, or an export sample)?

We'd like to close these points today if possible — procurement is on standby.

Thanks,
Acme Security
security@acme.com

--
Alice Liu (cc'd) — Acme Procurement
alice.liu@acme.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: security@acme.com, Alice Liu <alice.liu@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Sep 2025 12:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG — few clarifying Qs on data retention and training
Attachments: Redwood_SIG_Response_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOC2_TypeII_redacted.pdf (pdf)

Hi — thanks for the quick review and great questions. Quick answers up-front, followed by a short set of evidence and an offer to hop on a 20-minute call if helpful.

1) Prompt/log retention:
- Hosted API (default): ephemeral KV/prefix caches aside, prompt/request logs are retained for 30 days by default for debugging and abuse monitoring. Customers can configure longer retention (up to 365 days) for their own account via the Console; longer retention requires contract amendment for hosted customers and may incur additional encryption/audit controls.
- Dedicated / Private deployments: retention is customer-configurable. For Private deployments (VPC or on-prem), logs remain under customer control; Redwood does not retain copies unless explicitly contracted to provide managed logging.

2) Model training and customer data:
- We do NOT use customer prompts, outputs, attachments, or metadata to train or improve our public models. Aggregated telemetry (non-identifiable metrics like API error rates, token distributions) may be used for product improvement. Any use of customer-provided data for model training or research requires explicit opt-in and a written agreement.

3) Evidence you can share:
- Attached: redacted SOC2 Type II (focused on security and availability controls) and the completed SIG spreadsheet.
- Added a short note (data_handling_quicknote.pdf) summarizing retention defaults and configuration steps.

I'll leave Laura and Rishi on the thread for legal/compliance confirmation on the exact language and a redaction sample. Happy to schedule a short call to walk the InfoSec team through the docs.

Best,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: security@acme.com
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Sep 2025 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG — few clarifying Qs on data retention and training

Thanks Vivek — that helps. Two follow-ups from our InfoSec reviewer: 

A) For hosted customers, can you provide the configuration path (Console > Settings > ?) and an example API or Console screenshot showing where retention is set?
B) For Dedicated customers, can you confirm whether Redwood will ever request a copy of prompts for troubleshooting without a support ticket and customer approval?

If you can provide a one-page redacted export (no PII) that demonstrates the format of stored logs, that would be ideal for our intake.

Alice (Procurement) — we need this so our legal can finalize the SOW.

Regards,
Acme Security

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: security@acme.com, Alice Liu <alice.liu@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Sep 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG — few clarifying Qs on data retention and training
Attachments: data_handling_quicknote.pdf

Hi Alice / Acme Security — Laura and Rishi helped finalize the language; sending consolidated answers and the requested artifact.

A) Console path: Console > Organization > Data & Logs > Retention Policy. Default is 30 days for hosted accounts; toggles allow 90/180/365. We've included a screenshot mock (in the Drive link) and the API endpoints for retention configuration (GET/PUT /v1/orgs/{org_id}/retention). We can't paste the screenshot inline for security reasons but have added a redacted sample export to the Drive link.

B) Dedicated / Private troubleshooting: Redwood will not access customer prompt content from Dedicated or Private deployments without an explicit customer support ticket and written approval from the customer's admin. For Dedicated managed service customers we follow a documented escalation procedure — any access request must list scope, duration, and be logged to the customer's audit trail.

C) Export sample: shared a redacted sample export (no PII) to the Drive link and attached a short quicknote that explains the fields in the export and recommended redaction steps.

D) Training commitment: reiterating — no customer prompts/outputs are used to train our models unless the customer signs a data-use addendum. Aggregated telemetry is used internally under NDA and only in summarized forms.

If this meets your needs we can sign the SOW and set up onboarding. Happy to join a 20-minute call next week.

Thanks,
Vivek

--
Internal note: Laura/Legal — please confirm the exact redaction wording below for the SOW clause: "Redwood will not use customer-provided prompts, outputs, or attachments for model training without explicit, documented consent, and any such use will be subject to a separate data-use agreement and additional security review."

--
